A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Jeremiah Birrell's theoretical analysis of (f, Γ)-GANs. Their text, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and the core results can be matched despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical bounds and proofs, including in Appendices A–C. Statements about successful applications refer to prior work; no original experiments, simulations, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including the new Section 3.3 and Appendices A–F. Its discussion of neural networks and noise distributions does not report original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The divergence objective, generator formulation, and empirical GAN optimization problem are retained. v2 Equation (6) absorbs the existing shift parameter into the discriminator space, presenting an equivalent objective rather than changing the method.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The unbounded-support distributions discussed in v2 Section 3.3 are theoretical settings.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed method. References to IPM-GANs and other GAN approaches provide theoretical comparisons and research context.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures. Sample sizes and parameter dimensions appear as variables in mathematical bounds.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies. The small-variance noise discussion added in v2 Section 3.3 explains a theoretical implication without conducting a robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, error bars, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. The concentration inequalities and new complexity bound are formal theoretical results.

E6.justification: No measured numerical results, performance rankings, or qualitative evaluation outcomes are added or revised. The new analytical convergence rates are covered under T1.

T1.justification: v1 Section 1.1 explicitly leaves Rademacher-complexity bounds to existing literature. v2 Section 3.3 adds Assumption 3.10, Theorem 3.12, and a proof giving an entropy-integral bound for parameter-Lipschitz families with a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope. For a unit-ball parameter space in R^k, it obtains 48 sqrt(k/n) (E_P[L^2])^(1/2). The earlier concentration results and relocated proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add a substantive claimed contribution concerning distributions with unbounded support, including consistency guarantees under finite second moments for suitable network families and new insight for IPM-GANs. v1 concentrates on nonlinear-objective concentration inequalities and defers the corresponding complexity bounds.

C2.justification: v2 adds focused explanations of why the shift parameter cannot be absorbed into an IPM final-layer bias when comparing bounds (Remark 2.11), why Gaussian generator noise motivates unbounded-support analysis, and how small-variance unbounded perturbations affect the guarantee (Section 3.3). Existing interpretations of the core concentration bounds remain.

D1.justification: v2 Section 1 newly identifies the shift parameter with the discriminator's final-layer bias and presents Equation (6) as preferable for implementation. This supplies limited implementation guidance absent from v1, without documenting a changed algorithm.

R1.justification: v2 adds Biau et al. (2021) and van Handel (2016). Section 3.3 specifically contrasts its moment requirements with the sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential assumptions attributed to Biau et al. and Huang et al. The broader positioning relative to IPM-GANs is retained.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, and the document is substantially reorganized. Section 2 proofs and an error-decomposition proof move to Appendix D; v1 Section 3.3 becomes Appendix E; reverse-GAN results are collected in Appendix F. References move before the appendices, while the main text gains explanatory passages and the new Section 3.3.

P2.justification: Neither PDF contains figures or tables. v2 changes the title, author, and abstract layout, replaces the running preprint/date header with a horizontal rule, and changes typography and text/equation wrapping. The single-column mathematical presentation is retained.

improvement.justification: v1 makes consistency conditional on decaying Rademacher complexities and explicitly defers their bounds. v2 supplies a proved bound and explains its application to suitable network families with finite-second-moment data and noise, substantially strengthening the usefulness of the theory for unbounded support. The earlier results and proofs are retained, while the reorganized exposition and shift-parameter explanation improve accessibility.
